# Professor SOP This is the list of procedures, responsibilities, and duties of the [color=#cc74fc]Professor[/color] of this station.
The Professor is a senior role to all other [color=#cc74fc]Science[/color] personnel except the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Research Director[/bold][/color].
When selecting an Acting RD, the Professor should be considered above all other Science staff. Should the RD become incapacitated, the Professor should assume the role of acting head as soon as is convenient for the situation. The Professor as an acting head will fully assume the associated responsibilities, including ensuring the efficacy of the department as a whole instead of solely focusing on training.
The Professor shares all responsibilities of other Science staff but is to prioritize training, directing, and advising their staff, even during station-threatening events. To this end, the appropriate role's SOP should be consulted depending on whom the Professor instructs. Mind that the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Research Director[/bold][/color]'s orders are final on how the department will operate and what orders must be followed. Failure to perform these priorities or to act as a role model is grounds for demotion.
1. The Professor is expected to instruct [color=#cc74fc]Research Assistants[/color] on how to perform their duties and to guide other Science personnel should they ask for help. [bold]Research Assistants are to be prioritized first[/bold], but should the assistant decline help, the Professor does not need to focus their attention on them. The Professor should be open-minded to all available methods when teaching staff, even if it may not be the most familiar to the Professor.
2. The Professor is expected to fulfill the duties of other Science personnel [bold]if and only if[/bold] there are no Research Assistants needing to be instructed. In addition, when assuming other duties, the Professor is expected to follow the same SOP as the role they will perform. Due to the nature of [color=#cc74fc]Science[/color]'s work, it is [bold]highly[/bold] encouraged to step back and allow for [color=#cc74fc]Research Assistants[/color] to attempt performing tasks so long as there is no obvious danger in allowing them to do so, such as an artifact node that causes imminent doom or an explosion.
3. The Professor is expected to have a comprehensive understanding of the SOP and duties of each departmental role and may be consulted at any time regarding proper procedure. Additionally, the Professor must ensure their department is following SOP and is expected to remind staff and/or the department head to do so.
4. The Professor should be clearly distinguishable from other staff of their department, meaning that they ought to wear the appropriately designated clothing for their role. Consequently, the Professor should not give to other personnel any Nanotrasen property assigned to them except for instructional use or in case of station-threatening emergency.
5. The Professor is permitted to acquire surplus equipment and apparel of their department explicitly for training purposes.
6. The Professor may ask certain departmental personnel to vacate equipment for the sake of training. However, this request may be refused if there is an urgent need or if it would be unwise to vacate at that moment. Unreasonable refusal to vacate is grounds for disciplinary action should the department head find it necessary.
